title: Invariant affine shrinking for a finite locally free groupoid
statement: Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For $x\in U$ write $O(x)=t(s^{-1}(\{x\}))$ for its orbit; arrows can be compared and composed after extending their residue fields to a common field. Let $x\in U$ and suppose $O(x)$ is contained in an affine open subscheme of $U$. Then there is an affine open $W\subseteq U$ containing $O(x)$ and satisfying $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$ as open subschemes of $R$. No Noetherian, separatedness or dimension hypothesis on $U$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write O(y)=t(s⁻¹({y})). The identity and inverse laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme] make the arrow relation reflexive and symmetric. Given arrows r₁:y→z and r₂:z→v, apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-pullback-compatible-point], namely Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback, to (r₂,r₁) in R×_{s,U,t}R. The composition source and target equations evaluate at this point to give an arrow y→v. Thus the relation is transitive. By [def-pc-finite-locally-free], s is finite, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] makes O(x) finite. The identity puts x in O(x).

source.place: Tag 03JE (lemma-find-invariant-affine), proof, first paragraph and orbit equivalence

proof.text: Define H(E)=U\s(t⁻¹(U\E)) for each open E. It is open because t is continuous and s is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Membership means precisely that every arrow starting at y ends in E. The identity gives H(E)⊆E. The relation's symmetry and transitivity from step 1 give s⁻¹(H(E))=t⁻¹(H(E)). Transitivity also gives O(x)⊆H(E) whenever O(x)⊆E. Choose the affine open A of the hypothesis and set B=H(A). Then O(x)⊆B⊆A and B is invariant.

source.place: Tag 03JE (lemma-find-invariant-affine), proof, second paragraph, invariant open inside the chosen affine

proof.text: Use [def-pc-scheme] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to write A as Spec Γ(A). In the private helper finite_subset_basicOpen, form the ideal J of sections f whose basic open D_A(f) is contained in B. It is an ideal: D(0) is empty, D(f+g)⊆D(f)∪D(g), and D(af)=D(a)∩D(f). Pull the finite orbit back along the injective open immersion hA.fromSpec, obtaining a finite nonempty family T of prime ideals. For each q in T, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (IsAffineOpen.exists_basicOpen_le) gives f in J with f outside q, so J is contained in none of these primes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] (Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite, with both exceptional indices equal to a chosen member of T). Its contrapositive supplies f in J outside every q in T. IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_preimage_basicOpen then yields O(x)⊆D_A(f)⊆B.

source.place: Tag 03JE (lemma-find-invariant-affine), proof, choice of f by Algebra Tag 00DS (lemma-silly)

proof.text: Set W=H(D_A(f)). Step 2 gives O(x)⊆W⊆D_A(f)⊆B and s⁻¹(W)=t⁻¹(W). By the chosen orientation of H, W is already the complement of s(t⁻¹(U\D_A(f))). Intersecting it with B leaves W unchanged, since W⊆B. This is the exact complement-image formula needed by the norm-locus lemma; no inverse-image exchange remains to prove.

source.place: Tag 03JE (lemma-find-invariant-affine), proof, orbit description of the norm nonvanishing locus

proof.text: Apply [lem-pd-descent-norm-locus-affine] with its $V=U$, its affine open $A$ equal to ours, its open $W=B$, its section $f$ equal to ours, and its output open $U=W$. Its hypotheses hold: $s$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]; if $s(r)\in B$ then $t(r)\in B\subseteq A$ by invariance, giving $s^{-1}(B)\subseteq t^{-1}(A)$; step 3 gives $D_A(f)\subseteq B$; step 4 gives both $W\subseteq D_A(f)$ and the required complement-image formula. The lemma therefore makes $W$ affine. Its norm is formed on $B$ and restricted to the affine principal open $D_A(f)$; neither affineness of $B$ nor globally constant degree is needed. Finally step 4 gives $O(x)\subseteq W$ and invariance. Equal inverse-image open subsets determine equal open subschemes, as required.

source.place: Tag 03JE (lemma-find-invariant-affine), proof, final norm argument and affineness conclusion

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-619400a3b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against Stacks groupoids.tex Tag 03JE (lemma-find-invariant-affine). It has no new nodes, and the item statement is byte-identical to live and side-live (both still unsplit, no repair note). The item matches the source hypothesis by hypothesis: an absolute groupoid, s,t finite locally free, O(x) inside an affine open; the conclusion asks for an affine invariant W containing O(x), which is equivalent because an invariant open set containing x contains O(x). No target is weakened and no SGA is used. Step 1: reflexivity and symmetry come from e and i; transitivity composes field-valued arrows over a common field from lem-weil-common-extension-fields, and the finite fibre uses clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres (def-pc-finite-locally-free includes finite). Step 2: H(E)=U\t(s^-1(U\E)) is the source's W'; it is open by clause (1) applied to t, and I checked the direction of y in H(E) iff O(y) contained in E. Step 3: Tag 00DS through the basis clause (i) of lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open and lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance; the prime avoidance is applied to a finite nonempty family of primes, and D(f) is contained in B. Step 4: inversion swaps t(s^-1 Z) and s(t^-1 Z), which gives the complement formula. Step 5: lem-pd-descent-norm-locus-affine with V=U, A=A, W=B, U=W; its hypotheses are checked (s^-1(B) contained in t^-1(A) by invariance), and I checked the criterion itself: the norm is nonvanishing exactly on that set, which is a basic open of the affine D(f); empty fibres give norm 1. No affine intersections, Noetherian, separatedness or constant-rank hypotheses are used. Duplicate search (03JE / invariant affine): the pd descent-datum shrinking nodes and the parent codimension-one node are narrower, so none states this item. I accept the declared tool_uses lem-pd-descent-norm-locus-affine and lem-weil-common-extension-fields as generic black boxes.
